correctness.rationale: A generic integral one-parameter subgroup separates all N ambient characters; the Grassmannian has binom(N,d+1) coordinate fixed planes. A coordinate plane intersects the projective toric orbit closure iff it contains a coordinate fixed point indexed by a vertex: projective intersection is nonempty closed C*-stable and hence has a fixed point, while distinct weights force coordinate fixed points and toric orbit-limit vertices. Euler localization for a possibly singular projective complex variety applies; counting vertex-free index sets gives the formula. Veronese v=d+1 and Segre v=N follow. Independently checked subsets for bounded N; this is not an infinite proof. No smoothness or normality required.
